2 What phidentify is

“Are these two photos the same?” has no single answer. Two files can hold the same bytes, or the same encoded raw data with different keywords, or different bytes that Lightroom Classic would still accept as the same original. A whole-file checksum answers the first question and is silent on the others. A metadata comparison answers a fourth question and says nothing about pixels.

phidentify computes several named identities for a photo file, each answering one question:

Identity Rust field OCaml field Equal values mean
Whole-file SHA-256 sha256 sha256 every byte is equal
DNG encoded raw blocks dng_raw_blocks_sha256 dng_raw_blocks the same encoded primary raw data, under the same encoding tags
Lightroom Classic original fingerprint lightroom_digest lightroom Lightroom Classic’s original matcher would pair the files
Metadata record metadata_digest metadata equal exiftool-rs metadata records, file location left out
Preserved (complement) digest preserved_sha256, with dng_semantic_profile preserved, with dng_semantic every byte outside the primary XMP packet is equal, at the same size and layout
Image data image_data_sha256 image_data the same stored image bytes, in a camera raw, TIFF or JPEG that is not a DNG
Block marks block_marks_sha256 block_marks the same large blocks, by length and sampled ends, wherever they sit in the file

Beside the identities, phidentify can hand back a file’s skeleton: every byte outside those large blocks, with a map of where each block goes. A skeleton is not an identity. It is what rebuilds the file as it is now from a later version that a metadata edit has rewritten. The chapter on block marks and skeletons covers both.

Three rules hold for every identity, in every interface:

  1. They are separate. One identity never stands in for another. Equal raw blocks are not equal bytes; equal image data is not equal metadata; an equal Lightroom fingerprint is not equal pixels; an equal metadata record says nothing about image data.
  2. A missing identity is not a match. An identity that was not requested, does not apply to the file, or failed, is reported as such. Two files that both failed an identity have not matched on it.
  3. Every value comes from one consistent read. phidentify checks that the file did not change while it was identified. If it did, the whole result is an error.

2.1 Where it fits

This book is one of nine on the FirstPair photo tools. Each owns one part, and The FirstPair Photo Stack shows how they fit together.

  • tiffgraph walks a TIFF or DNG file’s structure under a fixed grammar and finds its editable XMP packet.
  • phidentify computes a photo’s identities: SHA-256, DNG raw blocks, image data, block marks, Lightroom fingerprint, metadata record and preserved digest, and the skeleton that rebuilds a file from an edited copy.
  • phindex keeps those identities and a skeleton for every file of a volume, aligns two volumes by content, and restores a file as it was before a metadata edit.
  • DNG Compare compares pairs and preserves one side byte for byte as deltas against the other, restorable even after the other side is edited, with a searchable metadata section, through dngc.
  • Semantic Unison synchronizes photo trees, sending metadata edits without resending image bytes, keeps the versions it replaces as small skeletons, and preserves what a shuttle disk brings into the same archives.
  • packdir keeps directories of small files as SQLite archives that still work like plain files.
  • Tursolite is the SQLite and Turso layer under packdir, DNG Compare and Mechanic.
  • diskproxy serves a folder as a virtual disk, such as previews with camera metadata spliced in, and captures ratings into sidecars.
  • Lightroom Repair repairs Lightroom Classic catalogs, previews and Sync without forging their state.

2.1.1 How phidentify serves them

phidentify is one of three sister projects that grew out of the same photo-archive work. Each owns a different piece.

  • dng-compare compares DNG archives: it pairs files across two trees, compares their raw samples, decodes when encodings differ, reports metadata differences, and preserves exact older versions as originals or verified deltas. phidentify’s raw-block identity is dng-compare’s dng-subset block comparison turned into a digest, and its metadata identity uses dng-compare’s exiftool-rs engine. Its manual is on the First Pair shelf.
  • tiffgraph is a pure-OCaml, bounded TIFF/DNG graph walker for stock OCaml and OxCaml. Under a fixed grammar it finds a DNG’s primary XMP packet, checks that nothing else the file declares lies inside it, and refuses anything outside the grammar with a reason. phidentify uses it to locate the region the preserved digest leaves out. Its manual is on the First Pair shelf.
  • Semantic Unison is a fork of the Unison file synchronizer that synchronizes DNG metadata separately from image bytes. Peers negotiate which tiffgraph grammar they trust, as the profiles org.firstpair.dng-xmp/0, /1 and /2, and Unison owns the SDE/0 definitions and proofs that a metadata transfer left every other byte alone. phidentify reproduces Unison’s SDE/0-preserved hash so that an index built outside Unison speaks the same identity. Its manual is on the First Pair shelf.

phidentify itself computes identities and nothing else. It does not compare trees, write files, touch catalogs, or synchronize anything.

Comparing trees is the job of its main consumer, phindex, which keeps every phidentify identity of every file under a directory tree in a resumable SQLite index. Since its version 0.2.0, phindex align accounts for the files of one indexed archive in another by these identities rather than by name, so copies that were moved, renamed, re-dated or had other metadata edited are still found. phindex also uses the image-data prefix test described below to add the image-data identity to an existing index without reading most files again. Its manual is on the First Pair shelf.

2.2 What it is not

  • Not a rendering identity. No identity here says that two files look the same after processing. Crop, white balance, profiles and develop settings live in metadata, and the raw-data identities ignore them.
  • Not a decoded-pixel identity, except inside the Lightroom fingerprint, which decodes for its own purpose and reports only Lightroom’s value.
  • Not a validator. A file that yields every identity is not thereby a correct DNG.
  • Not Lightroom. The Lightroom fingerprint is an independent reimplementation, qualified against values Lightroom Classic stored. It does not call Adobe code.
